Audio Player sketch · not the prototype Admin Site Volume

A working player, wired to real audio. Press play — it makes sound. One behavior shared by the admin preview and the ::blush/audio component, with everything the eye sees set by tokens the theme owns. The hard states are below; each one says whether it is real or simulated, because three of them need a server to misbehave and this page has none.

In the Admin

media detail — preview card

The case for building one at all. A native <audio controls> is drawn by the browser, ignores every token, and differs between Chrome, Firefox and Safari — so in a card in the Editorial theme it reads as a foreign object someone pasted in. Switch the theme and the scheme above: this one moves with them. It is still only a preview, so it stays small and does nothing but confirm you are looking at the right file.

On the Site

::blush/audio{src=…}

The same component, the same JavaScript, in an entry. The theme owns every value here — the two below set radius, accent, surface, both type families and the numeral font, and nothing in the player's own CSS reads an admin token. That is the contract worth getting right early: a theme that wants square corners and a mono clock should not have to replace the player to get them.

The two site palettes are fixed and do not follow the Light/Dark control above, on purpose: a site's light and dark are the theme's business and have nothing to do with which scheme an operator chose for the admin.

The Sepia Afternoon

The second take was the one. We had been at it since the light went orange across the kitchen floor, and by the time the tape was rolling again nobody was trying very hard, which is usually when it works.

Recorded at home, one microphone, January.

Focus the scrubber and press an arrow key. aria-valuetext is what a screen reader reads out here.

The Hard States

where a hand-built player falls apart

Each of these is its own player, independently operable. The two marked simulated need a server that misbehaves, which a single HTML file cannot provide — so the flag is faked and the handling is real.
